name: Pied Piper's House, Hamelin
name_zh: 哈默尔恩 · 捕鼠人之家
note: 传说 1284 年，一个穿彩衣的吹笛人吹着笛子把哈默尔恩的老鼠引进威悉河淹死，市民却赖掉了工钱，他就用笛声把全城一百三十个孩子带走，再也没有回来。格林兄弟收进了《德国传说》，勃朗宁写成英语世界人人会背的童诗。镇上这座文艺复兴时期的“捕鼠人之家”外墙刻着这段记载，旁边那条小巷至今不许奏乐，夏天的星期天广场上还会演这出戏
note_en: Legend says that in 1284 a piper in a coat of many colors piped the rats of Hamelin into the Weser to drown, and when the townspeople refused to pay him he piped away a hundred and thirty of their children, who were never seen again. The Brothers Grimm included it in their German Legends, and Robert Browning turned it into the children's poem every English speaker knows. An inscription on this Renaissance house, the Rattenfängerhaus, records the story; the lane beside it is still a street where no music may be played, and on summer Sundays the tale is acted out in the square

name: Münchhausen's birthplace, Bodenwerder
name_zh: 博登韦尔德 · 闵希豪森故居
note: 真实的闵希豪森男爵 1720 年生在威悉河边这座庄园里，在俄国军队里打过仗，退役回乡后最爱在饭桌上讲自己的离奇经历：骑着炮弹飞、拽着自己的辫子把自己和马拉出沼泽、马被城门劈成两半还照样喝水。1785 年拉斯伯把这些故事用英文出版，男爵从此成了“吹牛大王”，他本人却很生气。庄园现在是市政厅，里面有闵希豪森博物馆，花园里有他骑着半匹马喝水的喷泉
note_en: The real Baron Münchhausen was born in 1720 in this manor house on the Weser, fought in the Russian army, and back home loved to tell outrageous stories at dinner: riding a cannonball, pulling himself and his horse out of a bog by his own pigtail, his horse cut in half by a falling portcullis and still drinking. In 1785 Rudolf Erich Raspe published the tales in English, and the baron became the world's most famous liar, much to his annoyance. The manor is now the town hall, with a Münchhausen museum inside and a fountain in the garden showing him on half a horse

name: Town Musicians statue, Bremen
name_zh: 不来梅 · 不来梅的城市乐手雕像
note: 格林童话《不来梅的城市乐手》里，一头老驴、一条老狗、一只老猫和一只公鸡被主人嫌弃，结伴去不来梅当城市乐手，路上用叠罗汉吓跑了强盗——有意思的是，它们最后根本没走到不来梅。市政厅西侧这组叠在一起的铜像是 1953 年格哈德·马尔克斯做的，据说两手握住驴的前腿许愿就能实现，所以驴腿被摸得锃亮
note_en: In the Grimms' tale of the Bremen Town Musicians, an old donkey, dog, cat and rooster, all unwanted by their masters, set off together to become town musicians in Bremen and on the way scare off a band of robbers by climbing on each other's backs; the funny thing is that they never actually get to Bremen. This bronze stack of animals beside the town hall was made by Gerhard Marcks in 1953, and holding the donkey's front legs is supposed to make your wish come true, which is why they're polished to a shine

name: Sababurg
name_zh: 萨巴堡
prototype_of: 格林童话《睡美人》（《荆棘公主》）里那座被荆棘围住、一睡百年的城堡，在德国童话之路上就被认作是莱因哈特森林深处的这座萨巴堡。格林兄弟在附近的卡塞尔收集童话，城堡建于 14 世纪，后来荒废，四周确实长满了玫瑰和荆棘。现在是一家城堡酒店，旁边就是德国最古老的原始森林保护区之一
prototype_of_en: The thorn-wrapped castle where Sleeping Beauty (Little Briar-Rose, in the Grimms' version) sleeps for a hundred years is, on Germany's Fairy Tale Route, this castle deep in the Reinhardswald. The Grimms collected their tales in nearby Kassel, and the fourteenth-century castle, long a ruin, really was overgrown with roses and briars. It's now a castle hotel, next to one of the oldest primeval-forest reserves in Germany

name: Goethe House, Frankfurt
name_zh: 法兰克福 · 歌德故居
note: 歌德 1749 年 8 月 28 日正午出生在这座四层楼的房子里，他在自传《诗与真》开头就这样写，连当时的星象都记了下来。他在这里长大，小时候得到的木偶戏台后来成了《威廉·迈斯特》的灵感，《少年维特之烦恼》和《浮士德》的最初稿子也是在这里写的。房子在二战中被炸毁，战后按原样重建，祖母送的木偶戏台还在
note_en: Goethe was born in this four-story house at noon on 28 August 1749, as he tells us at the very start of his autobiography, Poetry and Truth, down to the position of the planets. He grew up here; the puppet theater he was given as a child later inspired Wilhelm Meister, and he wrote The Sorrows of Young Werther and the first drafts of Faust here. The house was bombed in the Second World War and rebuilt exactly as it was, and the puppet theater from his grandmother is still there

name: Goethe's House on the Frauenplan, Weimar
name_zh: 魏玛 · 歌德故居
note: 歌德从 1782 年起住在魏玛这座黄色大宅里，直到 1832 年去世，《亲和力》和《浮士德》第二部都是住在这里时写成的。书房、藏书室和他临终坐着的扶手椅都原样保留，几分钟路外就是席勒故居
note_en: Goethe lived in this big yellow house in Weimar from 1782 until his death in 1832, and wrote Elective Affinities and the second part of Faust while living here. His study, his library and the armchair he died in are kept as they were, and Schiller's house is a few minutes' walk away

name: Auerbachs Keller, Leipzig
name_zh: 莱比锡 · 奥尔巴赫地窖酒馆
note: 《浮士德》第一部里，魔鬼梅菲斯特带浮士德下到这家地窖酒馆，和一群醉醺醺的大学生喝酒取乐，用魔法让桌子流出葡萄酒。歌德在莱比锡念大学时常来，酒馆里还挂着 1625 年的壁画，画的是传说中浮士德骑着酒桶飞出地窖。今天它仍是一家餐馆，梅德勒拱廊入口两边立着浮士德、梅菲斯特和被施了魔法的大学生铜像
note_en: In Faust Part One, Mephistopheles takes Faust down into this cellar tavern to drink with a crowd of tipsy students, and makes wine flow from the table by magic. Goethe came here often when he was a student in Leipzig, and the tavern still has paintings from 1625 showing the legendary Faust riding out of the cellar on a barrel. It's still a restaurant, and bronze figures of Faust, Mephisto and the bewitched students flank its entrance in the Mädler arcade

name: Slaughterhouse-Five, Dresden
name_zh: 德累斯顿 · 五号屠场
note: 1945 年 2 月 13 日盟军轰炸德累斯顿时，二十二岁的美军战俘冯内古特就关在这片屠宰场里，躲在地下冻肉库里活了下来，出来时整座城已是一片焦土。二十多年后他把这段经历写进《五号屠场》，主人公比利·皮尔格林“在时间里脱了钩”。屠宰场旧址如今是德累斯顿会展中心，地下室偶尔开放参观
note_en: When the Allies firebombed Dresden on 13 February 1945, Kurt Vonnegut, a twenty-two-year-old American prisoner of war, was being held in this slaughterhouse complex; he survived in an underground meat locker and came out to find the city burned to the ground. More than twenty years later he put the experience into Slaughterhouse-Five, whose hero Billy Pilgrim has come 'unstuck in time'. The old slaughterhouse is now Dresden's trade fair grounds, and the cellar is occasionally opened for tours

name: Nollendorfplatz, Berlin
name_zh: 柏林 · 诺伦多夫广场
note: 1929 到 1933 年，英国作家衣修伍德住在广场旁边的诺伦多夫街 17 号，把魏玛末年夜夜笙歌、纳粹步步逼近的柏林写成了《别了，柏林》，后来改编成音乐剧和电影《歌厅》。楼上有一块纪念牌。同一时期凯斯特纳的《埃米尔擒贼记》里，偷了埃米尔钱的小偷也住进了这个广场边的旅馆，一大群柏林孩子在外面盯梢
note_en: From 1929 to 1933 the English writer Christopher Isherwood lived just off this square at Nollendorfstraße 17, and turned the Berlin of the last Weimar years, all-night cabarets with the Nazis closing in, into Goodbye to Berlin, which became the musical and film Cabaret; there's a plaque on the building. In Erich Kästner's Emil and the Detectives from the same years, the thief who stole Emil's money also takes a room in a hotel on this square, while a crowd of Berlin kids keep watch outside

name: Alexanderplatz, Berlin
name_zh: 柏林 · 亚历山大广场
note: 德布林 1929 年的《柏林，亚历山大广场》用电影剪辑一样的手法，写刚出狱的搬运工弗兰茨·毕伯科普夫想在这片喧闹的工人街区重新做个好人，却一次次被卷回黑道。小说把电车、广告、屠宰场和街头小调全拼了进去，是德语现代主义小说的代表，后来法斯宾德拍成了十五小时的电视剧。今天的广场是战后重建的，世界时钟下是柏林人最常约见的地方
note_en: Alfred Döblin's Berlin Alexanderplatz (1929) cuts between scenes like a film to follow Franz Biberkopf, a laborer just out of prison, as he tries to go straight in this noisy working-class quarter and is dragged back into crime again and again. It crams in trams, advertisements, slaughterhouses and street songs and is the great modernist novel in German; Fassbinder later made it into a fifteen-hour TV series. The square was rebuilt after the war, and the World Clock is where Berliners arrange to meet

name: Fontane monument, Neuruppin
name_zh: 新鲁平 · 冯塔纳纪念像
note: 冯塔纳 1819 年出生在新鲁平的一家药房里，后来写了五卷《勃兰登堡边区漫游记》，把家乡的湖泊、庄园和小城一一写遍，晚年又写出德国最好的婚姻小说《艾菲·布里斯特》：十七岁的艾菲嫁给比她大二十多岁的男爵，一段旧情让她身败名裂。城里这座纪念像让他坐在石头上，手拿帽子和手杖，像刚走完一段路
note_en: Theodor Fontane was born in 1819 in a pharmacy in Neuruppin; he went on to write five volumes of Wanderings through the March of Brandenburg, covering every lake, manor and small town of his home region, and late in life wrote Effi Briest, the great German novel of marriage, in which seventeen-year-old Effi marries a baron twenty years older and is ruined by an old affair. This monument shows him sitting on a rock with his hat and walking stick, as if resting halfway through a walk

name: Hans Fallada House, Carwitz
name_zh: 卡尔维茨 · 汉斯·法拉达故居
note: 1932 年的《小人物，怎么办？》写经济危机里一个小职员和妻子的挣扎，让法拉达一举成名，第二年他用稿费买下梅克伦堡湖区的这座农舍，种地养蜂，躲开纳粹柏林。战后他写出《柏林孤影》，出版前就去世了。故居是博物馆，他葬在村里
note_en: Little Man, What Now? (1932), about a young clerk and his wife struggling through the Depression, made Fallada famous, and the next year he used the money to buy this farmhouse in the Mecklenburg lakes, where he farmed and kept bees well away from Nazi Berlin. After the war he wrote Alone in Berlin and died before it came out. The house is a museum, and he is buried in the village

name: Buddenbrookhaus, Lübeck
name_zh: 吕贝克 · 布登勃洛克之家
note: 托马斯·曼把祖父母的这座大宅原样写进《布登勃洛克一家》，开头就是 1835 年全家坐在孟街这座房子的“风景厅”里。二十多年后他又写出《魔山》，一个汉堡青年上山探病，在达沃斯的疗养院一住七年。这里现在是曼氏兄弟纪念馆，正在扩建，去之前先查开放情况
note_en: Thomas Mann put his grandparents' house straight into Buddenbrooks, which opens in 1835 with the family gathered in the 'landscape room' of this house on the Mengstraße. Twenty-odd years later he wrote The Magic Mountain, in which a young man from Hamburg goes up to a Davos sanatorium for a visit and stays seven years. The house is a museum of Thomas and Heinrich Mann and is being expanded, so check whether it's open before you go

name: Rathausmarkt, Hamburg
name_zh: 汉堡 · 市政厅广场
note: 海涅年轻时在汉堡叔叔的银行里学过生意，爱上了堂妹，第一部诗集也在这里出版。1842 年一场大火烧掉了汉堡三分之一的老城，第二年他从巴黎回来探母，在长诗《德国，一个冬天的童话》里说重建中的汉堡像一只剪了一半毛的卷毛狗。今天的市政厅就是在火灾后的废墟上建起来的，广场边立着海涅的铜像
note_en: As a young man Heine learned the business in his uncle's bank in Hamburg, fell in love with his cousin, and published his first collection of poems here. In 1842 a great fire destroyed a third of the old city, and when he came back from Paris the next year to see his mother he wrote, in the long poem Germany. A Winter's Tale, that half-rebuilt Hamburg looked like a half-shorn poodle. The present town hall was built on the ground cleared by the fire, and a bronze statue of Heine stands on the square

name: Heine's birthplace, Düsseldorf
name_zh: 杜塞尔多夫 · 海涅出生地
note: 海涅 1797 年出生在杜塞尔多夫老城博尔克街的这座房子里。他的《歌集》里有德国人人会唱的《罗蕾莱》，舒曼、舒伯特为他的诗谱了几百首歌。他后来流亡巴黎，再也没能回家。故居现在是一家文学书店兼咖啡馆，经常办朗读会，楼前就是老城最热闹的酒吧街
note_en: Heinrich Heine was born in 1797 in this house on the Bolkerstraße in Düsseldorf's old town. His Book of Songs includes 'The Lorelei', which every German can sing, and Schumann and Schubert set hundreds of his poems to music. He later went into exile in Paris and never came home. The house is now a literary bookshop and café that often hosts readings, right on the old town's liveliest street of bars

name: Lorelei rock
name_zh: 罗蕾莱岩
note: 莱茵河在这里拐了个急弯、河道最窄最深，自古是船夫的险滩。海涅的诗《罗蕾莱》说，岩顶坐着一个金发少女，一边梳头一边唱歌，船夫只顾抬头看她，就撞上了礁石。这首诗谱成歌后传遍德国，马克·吐温在《海外浪游记》里说起初受不了，后来成了他最喜欢的曲子。从对岸的圣戈阿尔看过去最好，岩顶有观景台
note_en: Here the Rhine bends sharply and runs at its narrowest and deepest, and boatmen have always feared it. In Heine's poem 'The Lorelei', a golden-haired maiden sits on top of the rock combing her hair and singing, and the boatman, gazing up at her, sails straight into the rocks. Set to music, the poem spread all over Germany; Mark Twain says in A Tramp Abroad that he couldn't stand the tune at first and ended up liking it more than any other. The best view is from Sankt Goar across the river, and there's a lookout on top of the rock

name: Heidelberg Castle
name_zh: 海德堡城堡
note: 1878 年马克·吐温在海德堡住了好几个月，就住在城堡上方的旅馆里，写下《海外浪游记》的开头几章：内卡河峡谷、半毁的红砂岩城堡、晚上像“坠落的银河”一样的城市灯火，还有满脸决斗伤疤的大学生。他甚至说海德堡的夜景让人“需要时间考虑再下结论”。从老桥上看城堡，或者坐缆车上去，都能看到他描写的那片风景
note_en: Mark Twain spent several months in Heidelberg in 1878, staying at a hotel above the castle, and wrote the opening chapters of A Tramp Abroad here: the Neckar gorge, the half-ruined red sandstone castle, the city lights at night like 'a fallen Milky Way', and the students with their dueling scars. Heidelberg by night, he said, makes you take time before you give your verdict. Look up at the castle from the Old Bridge, or ride the funicular up, and you'll see the view he describes

name: Hermann Hesse Museum, Calw
name_zh: 卡尔夫 · 黑塞博物馆
note: 黑塞 1877 年生在黑森林边的卡尔夫，后来在小说里一再把它写成“格伯斯奥”。《在轮下》里被逼进神学院的少年汉斯就来自这样一座小城；中年写的《荒原狼》则是一个分裂的知识分子在城市里游荡的自白。市集广场上有黑塞博物馆，老桥上立着他的铜像
note_en: Hesse was born in 1877 in Calw, on the edge of the Black Forest, and kept writing about it under the name Gerbersau. Hans in Beneath the Wheel, pushed into a seminary until he breaks, comes from just such a town; Steppenwolf, written in middle age, is the confession of a split intellectual wandering a city at night. The Hesse museum is on the market square, and his bronze statue stands on the old bridge

name: E. T. A. Hoffmann House, Bamberg
name_zh: 班贝格 · E. T. A. 霍夫曼故居
note: 霍夫曼 1809 到 1813 年在班贝格剧院当乐长，就住在剧院对面这座窄楼里，也在这里开始写怪诞故事。后来的《沙人》写一个被童年噩梦缠住、爱上自动玩偶的大学生，《胡桃夹子与老鼠国王》则成了柴可夫斯基芭蕾的原作。故居是一座小纪念馆
note_en: Hoffmann was music director of the Bamberg theater from 1809 to 1813, lived in this narrow house opposite it, and began writing his uncanny tales here. The Sandman, which followed, is about a student haunted by a childhood nightmare who falls in love with a mechanical doll, and The Nutcracker and the Mouse King became Tchaikovsky's ballet. The house is a small museum

name: Burning Mountain, Dudweiler
name_zh: 达德魏勒 · 燃烧的山
note: 1770 年，二十一岁的歌德从斯特拉斯堡出发骑马游历，来到萨尔布吕肯附近，专门去看了这座“燃烧的山”：地下的煤层自 17 世纪起就一直在燃烧，裂缝里冒着硫磺味的热气，靴底都烫脚。他在自传《诗与真》里详细记下了这次参观。两百五十年后地火还没完全熄灭，林间小径边仍有冒热气的裂缝，还立着一块纪念歌德来访的牌子
note_en: In 1770 the twenty-one-year-old Goethe rode out from Strasbourg on a tour and came near Saarbrücken specially to see this 'burning mountain', where a coal seam underground had been on fire since the seventeenth century; sulfurous fumes rose from the cracks and the ground was hot through his boots. He describes the visit in detail in his autobiography, Poetry and Truth. Two hundred and fifty years later the fire still hasn't quite gone out: there are steaming fissures beside the woodland path, and a sign recalling Goethe's visit

name: Lottehaus, Wetzlar
name_zh: 韦茨拉尔 · 绿蒂故居
prototype_of: 1772 年歌德在韦茨拉尔的帝国法院实习，在舞会上认识了已经订婚的夏洛特·布夫，常来她家这座德意志骑士团的院子。两年后他把这段单恋写成《少年维特之烦恼》，维特第一次见到绿蒂，她正在这里给弟妹们切面包。院子还在，楼里是绿蒂故居纪念馆
prototype_of_en: In 1772 Goethe was a trainee at the imperial court in Wetzlar; at a ball he met Charlotte Buff, already engaged, and kept coming to her family's home in this Teutonic Order courtyard. Two years later he turned his hopeless love into The Sorrows of Young Werther, and when Werther first sees Lotte here she is cutting bread for her little brothers and sisters. The courtyard is still there, and the house is a museum to Lotte

name: Brocken
name_zh: 布罗肯峰
note: 传说每年 4 月 30 日夜里，女巫们骑着扫帚飞上哈尔茨山的最高峰布罗肯峰狂欢。《浮士德》第一部里，梅菲斯特就带浮士德上山赶这场瓦尔普吉斯之夜；歌德自己 1777 年冬天登过这座山。今天可以坐蒸汽小火车上山，山顶常年雾气弥漫
note_en: Legend says that on the night of 30 April the witches fly on their broomsticks to the Brocken, the highest peak in the Harz, for their revels. In Faust Part One, Mephistopheles takes Faust up the mountain for this Walpurgis Night, and Goethe himself climbed it in the winter of 1777. Today a steam train runs to the summit, which is wrapped in fog most of the year

name: Großer Stechlinsee
name_zh: 大施泰希林湖
note: 冯塔纳的最后一部小说《施泰希林》以这片湖命名：据说世界上哪里有大地震、火山爆发，这片平静的湖就会冒起水柱，有大事时还会飞出一只红公鸡。小说里的老贵族就住在湖边的庄园里，看着旧普鲁士慢慢退场。湖水清澈见底，环湖有步道，湖边的小村诺伊格洛布索有冯塔纳的纪念石
note_en: Fontane's last novel takes its name from this lake: whenever there's an earthquake or an eruption somewhere in the world, they say, a waterspout rises from its still surface, and when something truly great happens a red rooster flies up out of it. The old nobleman of the novel lives on an estate by its shore, watching the old Prussia fade away. The water is famously clear, a footpath runs round it, and the village of Neuglobsow lies on the shore

name: Erich Kästner Museum, Dresden
name_zh: 德累斯顿 · 埃里希·凯斯特纳博物馆
note: 凯斯特纳 1899 年生在德累斯顿新城，小时候常到舅舅家这座别墅的花园里玩，后来在回忆录里写过。他写的孩子总是机灵又仗义：《飞翔的教室》里寄宿学校的男孩们，《两个小洛特》里在夏令营认出彼此的双胞胎姐妹。别墅现在是他的博物馆，花园墙头坐着一尊少年凯斯特纳的铜像
note_en: Kästner was born in 1899 in Dresden's Neustadt and as a boy often played in the garden of this villa, which belonged to his uncle; he wrote about it in his memoir. His children are always quick and loyal: the boarding-school boys of The Flying Classroom, the twin sisters who recognize each other at summer camp in Lottie and Lisa. The villa is now his museum, and a bronze of the young Kästner sits on the garden wall

name: Hagen monument, Worms
name_zh: 沃尔姆斯 · 哈根像
note: 《尼伯龙根之歌》里，勃艮第国王们的宫廷就在莱茵河边的沃尔姆斯：屠龙英雄齐格弗里德来这里求娶克里姆希尔德，后来被哈根刺死，哈根又把尼伯龙根宝藏沉进了莱茵河。河岸上这尊 1905 年的铜像就是哈根抛宝的那一刻，城墙边还有一座尼伯龙根博物馆
note_en: In the Nibelungenlied, the Burgundian kings hold court at Worms on the Rhine: the dragon-slayer Siegfried comes here to win Kriemhild, is later killed by Hagen, and Hagen sinks the Nibelung treasure in the Rhine. This bronze of 1905 on the riverbank shows him at the moment he throws the hoard in, and there's a Nibelungen museum in the towers of the city wall nearby

name: Hölderlin Tower, Tübingen
name_zh: 图宾根 · 荷尔德林塔
note: 荷尔德林写完书信体小说《许佩里翁》后精神失常，1807 年起被一位木匠收留在内卡河边这座塔楼里，在这里度过了后半生的三十六年，直到 1843 年去世，窗外就是河。塔楼现在是他的纪念馆，从对岸的梧桐树岛上看过去最好，夏天河上撑着长篙的平底船
note_en: After writing his novel in letters, Hyperion, Hölderlin lost his mind, and from 1807 a carpenter took him into this tower on the Neckar, where he lived for the last thirty-six years of his life, until 1843, with the river under his window. The tower is now a museum to him; the best view is from the plane-tree island opposite, and in summer punts are poled along the river below

name: Kleist's grave, Wannsee
name_zh: 柏林万湖 · 克莱斯特墓
note: 1811 年 11 月 21 日，克莱斯特和身患绝症的女友亨丽埃特·福格尔在小万湖边双双开枪自尽，就葬在出事的地方。他生前不得志，死后才被奉为德语最好的小说家之一：《O 侯爵夫人》开头是一则惊人的启事，《米夏埃尔·科尔哈斯》写马贩子为讨公道烧城造反。万湖是哈弗尔河的湖湾
note_en: On 21 November 1811 Kleist and his terminally ill friend Henriette Vogel shot themselves on the shore of the Kleiner Wannsee, and they are buried where it happened. Little recognized in his lifetime, he is now counted among the finest storytellers in German: The Marquise of O opens with an astonishing newspaper notice, and Michael Kohlhaas follows a horse dealer who burns towns in his fight for justice. The Wannsee is a bay of the Havel

name: Büchner's birthplace, Goddelau
name_zh: 戈德劳 · 毕希纳故居
note: 毕希纳 1813 年生在这座木筋房子里，只活了二十三岁，留下的作品却改变了德语文学：《伦茨》写一位诗人在山里一步步陷入疯狂，没写完的《沃伊采克》写一个穷士兵被人折磨到杀死爱人，是第一部以底层人为主角的悲剧。故居现在是毕希纳纪念馆
note_en: Büchner was born in this half-timbered house in 1813 and lived only twenty-three years, but what he left changed German writing: Lenz follows a poet sliding into madness in the mountains, and the unfinished Woyzeck, about a poor soldier tormented until he kills the woman he loves, is the first tragedy with a man from the bottom of society as its hero. The house is now a Büchner museum

name: Market square, Leipzig
name_zh: 莱比锡 · 集市广场
prototype_of: 1824 年 8 月 27 日，退伍士兵约翰·克里斯蒂安·沃伊采克因为嫉妒刺死情人，在莱比锡老市政厅前的集市广场上被公开斩首，围观的人成千上万。法庭为他是否精神失常争论了好几年，毕希纳读了医生的鉴定报告，写成剧本《沃伊采克》。广场今天是莱比锡老城的中心
prototype_of_en: On 27 August 1824 Johann Christian Woyzeck, a former soldier who had stabbed his lover in a fit of jealousy, was publicly beheaded on this market square in front of the Old Town Hall, before a crowd of thousands. The courts had argued for years over whether he was insane, and Büchner read the doctor's report and made it into his play Woyzeck. The square is still the heart of Leipzig's old town

name: Osthofen concentration camp memorial
name_zh: 奥斯特霍芬集中营纪念馆
prototype_of: 纳粹上台后，莱茵黑森的奥斯特霍芬在一座旧造纸厂里设了最早的集中营之一，关押政敌。流亡中的安娜·西格斯把它写成小说里的韦斯特霍芬集中营：七个囚犯越狱，营长砍了七棵梧桐树做成十字架，等着把抓回来的人钉上去。旧厂房现在是纪念馆和纳粹史档案中心
prototype_of_en: Soon after the Nazis came to power, one of the first concentration camps for their opponents was set up in an old paper factory at Osthofen in Rhenish Hesse. Anna Seghers, in exile, made it the Westhofen camp of her novel, where seven prisoners escape and the commandant has seven plane trees cut into crosses to hang them on once they're caught. The old factory is now a memorial and documentation center on the Nazi era

name: Günter Grass House, Lübeck
name_zh: 吕贝克 · 君特·格拉斯之家
note: 格拉斯 1959 年的《铁皮鼓》让战后德国文学重新被世界看见：三岁时决定不再长大的奥斯卡，敲着铁皮鼓看完了但泽和纳粹的年代。1999 年他获诺贝尔奖，晚年住在吕贝克附近。老城里这座房子是格拉斯之家，展出他的手稿，也展出他的版画和雕塑，后院有雕塑花园
note_en: Grass's The Tin Drum (1959) put postwar German writing back in front of the world: Oskar, who decides at three never to grow any bigger, drums his way through Danzig and the Nazi years. Grass won the Nobel Prize in 1999 and spent his last years near Lübeck. This house in the old town is the Günter Grass House, showing his manuscripts as well as his prints and sculptures, with a sculpture garden behind

name: Krabat Mill, Schwarzkollm
name_zh: 施瓦茨科尔姆 · 克拉巴特磨坊
note: 克拉巴特是劳齐茨地区索布人的传说人物，普鲁士勒把他写成《鬼磨坊》：少年乞丐一连三夜梦见有声音叫他去施瓦茨科尔姆的磨坊，结果成了黑魔法师的学徒。他也写了《小幽灵》等童书。村边这座磨坊是按传说重建的，夏天有露天戏剧，磨坊和小博物馆都能参观
note_en: Krabat is a figure of Sorbian legend in Lusatia, and Preußler turned him into The Satanic Mill: a beggar boy dreams three nights running that a voice is calling him to the mill at Schwarzkollm, and becomes the apprentice of a black magician. Preußler also wrote The Little Ghost and other children's books. This mill at the edge of the village was rebuilt after the legend, with open-air theater in summer, and the mill and a small museum can be visited

name: Michael Ende Park, Garmisch-Partenkirchen
name_zh: 加尔米施-帕滕基兴 · 米切尔·恩德公园
note: 米切尔·恩德 1929 年生在阿尔卑斯山脚下的加尔米施。他的《毛毛》写一个住在圆形剧场废墟里、最会倾听的小女孩，和偷走人们时间的灰先生作战；《吉姆·纽扣》则是火车头卢卡斯和黑人男孩吉姆的冒险。这座疗养公园以他命名，有露天剧场、草坪迷宫和他书里的巨龟莫拉
note_en: Michael Ende was born in 1929 in Garmisch at the foot of the Alps. Momo is about a little girl who lives in the ruins of an amphitheater, listens better than anyone, and takes on the grey men who steal people's time; Jim Button follows the engine driver Luke and the boy Jim on their adventures. This spa park is named after him, with an open-air stage, a lawn maze and the ancient turtle Morla from his books

name: Eulenspiegel Museum, Mölln
name_zh: 默尔恩 · 蒂尔·欧伊伦施皮格尔博物馆
prototype_of: 蒂尔·欧伊伦施皮格尔是中世纪德国传说里专门捉弄人的小丑，传说他 1350 年死在默尔恩，教堂外墙上还有他的墓碑。克尔曼的《蒂尔》把他挪到了三十年战争，让他在烧杀和瘟疫里一路杂耍。市集广场上有他的铜像，旁边这座老房子是欧伊伦施皮格尔博物馆
prototype_of_en: Till Eulenspiegel is the trickster jester of medieval German legend, said to have died in Mölln in 1350, and his gravestone is still on the church wall. Kehlmann's Tyll moves him into the Thirty Years' War and has him juggle his way through its burning and plague. His bronze stands on the market square, and this old house beside it is the Eulenspiegel Museum

name: Göttingen Observatory
name_zh: 哥廷根大学天文台
note: 数学家高斯 1807 年起当哥廷根天文台台长，在这里住到 1855 年去世，几乎一辈子没离开过这座城。克尔曼的《丈量世界》把他和到处探险的洪堡写成一对：一个坐在家里算出世界，一个跑遍美洲去量它。古典主义风格的天文台楼保存完好，现在是大学的研究院
note_en: The mathematician Gauss became director of the Göttingen Observatory in 1807 and lived here until his death in 1855, hardly ever leaving the town. Kehlmann's Measuring the World pairs him with the explorer Humboldt: one stays at home and works out the world, the other travels the Americas to measure it. The neoclassical observatory building survives intact and now houses a university institute

name: Weißer Hirsch, Dresden
name_zh: 德累斯顿 · 白鹿区
note: 易北河北岸山坡上的白鹿区满是十九世纪的别墅和疗养院。特尔坎普在这里长大，《塔》写的就是民主德国最后七年里住在这片别墅区的医生、出版人和学者，他们守着旧家具和藏书，像活在另一个世纪，直到 1989 年一切崩塌。今天可以坐缆车从易北河边上来
note_en: The Weißer Hirsch quarter on the slopes above the Elbe is full of nineteenth-century villas and old sanatoriums. Tellkamp grew up here, and The Tower follows the doctors, publishers and scholars living in these villas through the last seven years of East Germany, holding on to their old furniture and books as if in another century until everything collapses in 1989. A funicular brings you up from the Elbe

name: Marzahn, Berlin
name_zh: 柏林 · 马灿
note: 马灿是东柏林边上民主德国时代建起的大片预制板住宅区。赫恩多夫的《契克》就从这里出发：十四岁的迈克家住马灿的一座别墅，暑假被父母丢下，俄罗斯转学生契克开来一辆偷来的拉达，两人不带地图就开进了勃兰登堡乡下。登上高楼的观景台能看到一整片板楼
note_en: Marzahn, on the eastern edge of Berlin, is a vast estate of prefabricated housing built in East German times. Herrndorf's Why We Took the Car sets out from here: fourteen-year-old Maik, whose family has a villa in Marzahn, is left alone for the summer, and Tschick, the new boy from Russia, turns up in a stolen Lada, and the two of them drive off into the Brandenburg countryside with no map. From the skywalk on top of a tower block you can see the whole sea of slab buildings

name: Emmertsgrund, Heidelberg
name_zh: 海德堡 · 埃默茨格伦德
note: 1992 年，十四岁的斯坦尼西奇随家人逃离波黑战争来到海德堡，住进山坡上的高楼区埃默茨格伦德。《出身》里写，这里最出力帮外来孩子融入的，是一座破旧的阿拉尔加油站，大家天天在那儿混。这片住宅区离海德堡老城不远，站在坡上能望见莱茵平原
note_en: In 1992, at fourteen, Stanišić fled the war in Bosnia with his family and came to Heidelberg, to the high-rise estate of Emmertsgrund on the hillside. In Where You Come From, the institution that does most to help the newcomers fit in is a run-down Aral petrol station where everyone hangs out. The estate is not far from the old town, and from the slope you look out over the Rhine plain

name: Old Anatomy, Ingolstadt
name_zh: 因戈尔施塔特 · 老解剖楼
note: 《弗兰肯斯坦》里，日内瓦青年维克多来到因戈尔施塔特上大学，迷上了生命的秘密，在这里拼出了那个怪物。这所大学当时是巴伐利亚最古老的大学，医学和解剖很有名。大学的老解剖楼建于 18 世纪，现在是德国医学史博物馆，后面还有一座药草园
note_en: In Frankenstein, Victor comes from Geneva to study at the university of Ingolstadt, becomes obsessed with the secret of life, and puts his creature together here. It was then the oldest university in Bavaria, with a well-known medical faculty. The university's eighteenth-century anatomy building is now the German Museum of Medical History, with a medicinal herb garden behind it

name: Dachau concentration camp memorial
name_zh: 达豪集中营纪念馆
note: 《偷书贼》的小镇莫尔兴在慕尼黑附近，是虚构的，书里的达豪集中营却是真的：犹太囚犯被押着穿过小镇去达豪，养父汉斯给一个老人递了块面包，两人都挨了鞭子。藏在地下室的马克斯后来也被送进这里。集中营是纳粹最早建的一座，如今是纪念馆，免费参观
note_en: Molching, the little town near Munich in The Book Thief, is invented, but the Dachau camp in the book is real: Jewish prisoners are marched through the town on their way there, and when Liesel's foster father Hans hands an old man a piece of bread, both are whipped. Max, hidden in the basement, is later sent here too. One of the first camps the Nazis built, it is now a memorial, free to visit
coord_checked: Dachau concentration camp memorial site (Wikimedia Commons) — https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/Category:Dachau_concentration_camp_memorial_site

name: Checkpoint Charlie, Berlin
name_zh: 柏林 · 查理检查站
note: 冷战时，弗里德里希街上的查理检查站是东西柏林之间最有名的过境点。勒卡雷的《柏林谍影》开头，英国驻柏林情报站长利玛斯在检查站熬了一夜，等最后一名特工从东边过来，却眼看他在边境线前被枪杀。今天路中间还立着复制的岗亭，旁边有柏林墙博物馆
note_en: During the Cold War, Checkpoint Charlie on the Friedrichstraße was the best-known crossing between East and West Berlin. The Spy Who Came in from the Cold opens with Leamas, the head of British intelligence in Berlin, waiting all night at the checkpoint for his last agent to come over from the East, only to watch him shot down short of the line. A replica guard hut stands in the middle of the street, and the Wall Museum is beside it

name: Schiller's House, Weimar
name_zh: 魏玛 · 席勒故居
note: 席勒年轻时写《强盗》《阴谋与爱情》，一个贵族青年爱上乐师的女儿，被宫廷阴谋逼死，台下观众都哭了。1799 年他搬到魏玛，和歌德成了挚友，第二年写成《玛利亚·斯图亚特》。1802 年起他住在这座黄房子里，1805 年在这里去世，阁楼书房和他的书桌都还在
note_en: As a young man Schiller wrote The Robbers and Intrigue and Love, in which a young nobleman's love for a musician's daughter is destroyed by court intrigue, and audiences wept. In 1799 he moved to Weimar, became Goethe's close friend, and finished Mary Stuart the next year. From 1802 he lived in this yellow house, where he died in 1805; his attic study and desk are still there

name: Lessing House, Wolfenbüttel
name_zh: 沃尔芬比特尔 · 莱辛故居
note: 莱辛 1770 年起在沃尔芬比特尔当公爵图书馆馆长，晚年住在图书馆旁这座房子里，1779 年写成《智者纳旦》：一个犹太商人用三枚戒指的寓言回答苏丹，劝三大宗教彼此宽容。他早年的《明娜·冯·巴尔赫姆》是德语最早的喜剧杰作。故居现在是纪念馆，隔壁就是奥古斯特公爵图书馆
note_en: Lessing became librarian of the ducal library at Wolfenbüttel in 1770 and in his last years lived in this house beside it, where in 1779 he wrote Nathan the Wise: a Jewish merchant answers the Sultan with the parable of the three rings and pleads for tolerance between the three faiths. His earlier Minna von Barnhelm was the first great comedy in German. The house is a museum, next door to the Herzog August Library

name: Theodor Storm House, Husum
name_zh: 胡苏姆 · 施托姆故居
note: 施托姆 1817 年生在北海边的小城胡苏姆，称它是“海边的灰色小城”。他最后的中篇《白马骑士》写北弗里斯兰的一个堤长骑着白马修新堤，与洪水和村民的迷信对抗，传说风暴夜里还能看见他的白马在堤上奔跑。他住过的这座房子现在是施托姆博物馆
note_en: Storm was born in 1817 in Husum on the North Sea, which he called 'the grey town by the sea'. His last novella, The Rider on the White Horse, tells of a North Frisian dikemaster who builds a new dike on his white horse against floods and the villagers' superstitions; on stormy nights, they say, his horse can still be seen galloping on the dike. The house where he lived is now the Storm museum

name: Remarque Peace Centre, Osnabrück
name_zh: 奥斯纳布吕克 · 雷马克和平中心
note: 雷马克 1898 年生在奥斯纳布吕克，十八岁应征入伍，上了西线。1929 年的《西线无战事》用一个年轻士兵的口吻写战壕里的死亡，被纳粹焚毁，却成了全世界读得最多的反战小说。他的《黑色方尖碑》把家乡写成小城维尔登布吕克。市集广场边的这座楼是雷马克和平中心
note_en: Remarque was born in Osnabrück in 1898, was called up at eighteen and sent to the Western Front. All Quiet on the Western Front (1929) tells of death in the trenches in the voice of a young soldier; the Nazis burned it, and it became the most widely read antiwar novel in the world. In The Black Obelisk he turned his home town into the little town of Werdenbrück. This building on the market square is the Remarque Peace Centre

name: Berliner Ensemble
name_zh: 柏林剧团
note: 1928 年布莱希特的《三分钱歌剧》在施普雷河边这座剧院首演，一炮而红。流亡归来后，他和妻子海伦妮·魏格尔 1949 年创办柏林剧团，魏格尔演的《大胆妈妈》推着货车在三十年战争里做买卖、一个个失去孩子，成了剧团的招牌。1954 年剧团搬进这里，门前广场上有布莱希特的坐像
note_en: Brecht's Threepenny Opera opened in this theater by the Spree in 1928 and was an instant hit. Back from exile, he and his wife Helene Weigel founded the Berliner Ensemble in 1949, and Weigel's Mother Courage, hauling her cart through the Thirty Years' War and losing her children one by one, became the company's signature. The company moved in here in 1954, and Brecht sits in bronze on the square in front

name: Bonn Hauptbahnhof
name_zh: 波恩火车总站
note: 伯尔的《小丑之见》里，丑角汉斯·施尼尔丢了工作也丢了爱人，回到当时西德首都波恩的公寓，整夜打电话求人。小说最后，他抹上白脸、抱着吉他，坐在波恩火车站的台阶上卖唱，等玛丽从罗马回来。这座红砖站房是 19 世纪末的老建筑，至今还在用
note_en: In Böll's The Clown, the clown Hans Schnier, out of work and abandoned by the woman he loves, comes back to his flat in Bonn, then the West German capital, and spends the night on the phone begging for help. At the end he paints his face white, takes his guitar and sits on the steps of Bonn station singing for coins, waiting for Marie to come back from Rome. The red station building dates from the late nineteenth century and is still in use

name: Old University, Heidelberg
name_zh: 海德堡 · 老大学
note: 《朗读者》里十五岁的米夏埃尔爱上了比他大二十岁的汉娜，几年后在法学院的研讨课上，竟在纳粹集中营看守的审判席上认出了她。书里没写城名，海德堡市官方说故事就发生在这里，施林克本人也在海德堡读法律。大学广场上的老大学楼里有大学博物馆和学生禁闭室
note_en: In The Reader, fifteen-year-old Michael falls in love with Hanna, twenty years older; years later, at a law-school seminar, he recognizes her in the dock at the trial of concentration-camp guards. The book never names its city, but Heidelberg says the story is set here, and Schlink himself studied law in Heidelberg. The Old University on the university square has the university museum and the old student prison
